claims.statement: For persistent ITP of only several months without severe bleeding and with feasible medical care, elective splenectomy should be deferred until at least one year after diagnosis when possible.
claims.limitation: Current ASH summary governs; conditional on feasibility and not an absolute prohibition on urgent surgery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults several months into persistent ITP with reliable hematology follow-up and no major bleeding.

claims.statement: A patient with known or credibly documented malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility requires advance planning for trigger-free anaesthesia in a facility prepared to manage malignant hyperthermia.
claims.limitation: Evidence relies substantially on expert opinion and case reports; no clinic anaesthetic, crisis algorithm, or dantrolene dose is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with known or credibly documented malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility.

claims.statement: A persistent palpable breast finding in an adult at least 40 years old warrants targeted ultrasonography of the exact clinical area when diagnostic mammography is negative.
claims.limitation: Single current specialty guideline; this does not endorse blanket supplemental screening ultrasound for breast density alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults age 40 or older with a persistent palpable breast finding and negative diagnostic mammography.

claims.statement: Pregnancy testing for hCG is part of the assessment of reproductive-age pelvic or abdominal pain when pregnancy is possible; menstrual history or reported contraception does not substitute for testing when early-pregnancy complications are suspected.
claims.limitation: Guideline and independent government test information. The authored task selects testing as part of immediate assessment; it does not postpone urgent care, select a universal urine-versus-serum assay, or diagnose an ectopic pregnancy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Reproductive-age adults with pelvic/abdominal symptoms and possible pregnancy.

claims.statement: For an otherwise asymptomatic patient with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, age under 50 years is an independent guideline criterion supporting parathyroidectomy.
claims.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. Operative suitability, localization, genetic evaluation, and all other surgical criteria remain outside this focused pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults younger than 50 years with confirmed asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism and no other operative criterion described in this pathway.

claims.statement: For an adult with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, skeletal assessment includes DXA at the lumbar spine, hip, and distal one-third radius.
claims.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. This claim does not assign a universal DXA diagnostic threshold or determine surgery by bone density alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism undergoing standard skeletal assessment.

claims.statement: Positive predictive value uses all positive test results as its denominator and depends on prevalence in the tested population as well as on sensitivity and specificity.
claims.limitation: The direction exercises assume sensitivity, specificity, and the testing process remain fixed while prevalence changes.
claims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

claims.statement: When operative resection is selected for resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the body or tail, the anatomic pancreatic resection is a distal pancreatectomy rather than a pancreaticoduodenectomy.
claims.limitation: This location-based operation does not determine treatment sequencing or establish resectability by itself.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the pancreatic body or tail who are selected to proceed with operative resection.

claims.statement: Sensitivity is the proportion testing positive among reference-positive cases, while specificity is the proportion testing negative among reference-negative cases.
claims.limitation: The fictional reference classification is treated as correct solely for teaching the denominators.
claims.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

claims.statement: Tissue pathology is required to diagnose and classify suspected PTLD; EBV DNA and imaging are supportive and do not replace histopathologic diagnosis.

claims.applicablePopulation: Transplant recipients with suspected PTLD.
